Avalanche.title: Avalanche vs snowball: which debt should you pay first?
Avalanche.desc:
Three debts, $12,500 in total: a $3,000 card at 22%, a $1,500 card at 18% and an $8,000 car loan at 7%. Minimums only: over 4 years and $3,410 of interest.

Add $300 a month:
Avalanche (highest rate first): 22 months, $1,163 interest.
Snowball (smallest balance first): 22 months, $1,203 interest, but the first debt is gone in 5 months, not 9.

Both beat the minimums by over $2,200. From Episode 2, Interest works both ways.
Illustration: minimums $335 a month plus $300 extra, monthly compounding. Not financial advice.
#debt #debtfree #avalanche #snowball #personalfinance #shorts

ZeroTrap.title: The 0% offer trap: $3,000 at $150 a month
ZeroTrap.desc:
0% for 12 months sounds free, and it can be, if you clear it in time. Spend $3,000 and pay $150 a month: $1,200 is still owed when the offer ends. At 22% after that, it takes 9 more months and about $110 of interest.

The fix: divide the balance by the months you have. $3,000 over 12 months is $250 a month.
Illustration: 0% for 12 months, then 22% APR compounded monthly. Check your card's terms. Not financial advice.
#creditcard #0percent #debt #personalfinance #shorts

StopPaying.title: Stop paying a $5,000 credit card: it's $14,872 in 5 years
StopPaying.desc:
A $5,000 balance at 22%, compounded monthly, with no payments: interest is added every month, then charged interest too. After 2 years it's about $7,700. After 5 years, $14,872: nearly triple, without spending another cent.

Illustration: 22% APR compounded monthly, no payments and no fees. Penalty rates and fees can make it worse. Not financial advice.
#creditcard #debt #compoundinterest #personalfinance #shorts

LumpSum.title: $10,000 invested once, never touched for 40 years
LumpSum.desc:
$10,000, invested once and never touched, at 7% a year:
10 years: $20,097
20 years: $40,387
30 years: $81,165
40 years: $163,114

It doubles roughly every 10 years, and each doubling is bigger than the last.
Illustration only: assumes a steady 7% yearly return, compounded monthly, before fees, tax and inflation. Real returns vary. Not financial advice.
#investing #compoundinterest #money #personalfinance #shorts

BlackFriday.title: Black Friday: 50% off isn't saving if it wasn't on your list
BlackFriday.desc:
A $400 item at 50% off: $200. If it wasn't on your list, you didn't save $200. You spent $200. Invested instead at 7% for 20 years, that $200 becomes about $808.

A discount only saves money on what you'd buy anyway. Make the list before the sale.
Illustration only: assumes a steady 7% yearly return, compounded monthly, before fees, tax and inflation. Not financial advice.
#blackfriday #saving #money #personalfinance #shorts

Holiday.title: $1,000 of holiday gifts on a 22% card: minimum vs $100 a month
Holiday.desc:
$1,000 of holiday shopping on a 22% credit card.
Pay the minimum: almost 6 years to clear, $766 of interest.
Pay $100 a month: gone in 12 months, $115 of interest.
Same gifts, $651 apart.

Illustration: 22% APR, compounded monthly. Minimum = month's interest + 1% of balance (at least $25). Real card terms vary. Not financial advice.
#holidays #creditcard #debt #personalfinance #shorts

RealRaise.title: A 2% raise with 4% inflation: $50,000 after 5 years
RealRaise.desc:
2% raises every year, while prices rise 4% a year. On a $50,000 salary, after 5 years your payslip says $55,204. In today's money, that buys what $45,374 buys now. You're going backwards.

A real raise beats inflation. Check the number, not just the raise.
Illustration: steady 2% raises and 4% inflation a year. Real figures vary. Not financial advice.
#inflation #salary #money #personalfinance #shorts
